questions.question: Explain why places near the equator are hot and places near the poles are cold.
questions.expected_answer: Because the Earth is round, the sun's rays hit places near the equator almost straight on, so the energy is concentrated on a small area and heats it a lot. Near the poles, the rays arrive at a low slant, so the same energy is spread over a bigger area and passes through more atmosphere, so each place gets less heat and is colder.

questions.question: Describe what January and July temperature maps show about the seasons.
questions.expected_answer: On the January map, the Southern Hemisphere is in summer and places such as southern Africa and Australia are warm, while North America, Europe and northern Asia are cold. On the July map, the colours swap: the Northern Hemisphere has summer and places like North Africa are very hot, while southern Africa has winter. Near the equator it stays hot all year. The seasons are opposite because the Earth is tilted as it travels around the sun.

questions.question: Name three factors other than distance from the equator that affect temperature, with examples.
questions.expected_answer: Altitude: higher places are colder, so Kilimanjaro has snow near the equator and Johannesburg has colder winters than Durban. Distance from the sea: coastal places have milder temperatures than places far inland like Upington. Ocean currents: the warm Agulhas Current makes Durban warmer, and the cold Benguela Current makes the west coast cooler.
